reasons.A: Clipped staccato sentences in long runs of 'He said. He did.' are nothing like the author's loose, qualified, digressive clauses, despite some period diction.
reasons.B: Long, hedged, chatty sentences with asides ('I dare say', 'so to speak'), a mid-sentence dash and a semicolon come closest to the author's confiding, slightly fussy movement and old-fashioned register.
reasons.C: Plain, modern, evenly paced prose with a flat stance; it has little of the author's wordy qualifiers, period feel or conversational asides.
reasons.D: Period register and semicolon-joined, wry sentences fit well, but the neat antithetical cadences ('rather not have him to dinner... next door') are more polished and epigrammatic than the author's rambling, button-holing manner.
